items.title: Draft Taxi Licensing Policy
items.time: Closes at 12 noon on Thursday 26 November 2026, as stated on the council's consultations page.
items.plain: The council is updating the rules for taxi and private hire drivers, vehicles and operators. Changes are marked in red in the draft policy.
items.detail: Neath Port Talbot Council licenses hackney carriage and private hire drivers, vehicles and operators across the county borough. The revised policy (August 2026) sets the standards and procedures the council uses when deciding licence applications. The council asks residents, the licensed trade and partner organisations for comments.
items.how: Read the revised policy (PDF) and comment through the 'Have your say' link on the council's consultations page before 12 noon on 26 November 2026.

people: Taxi and private hire drivers and operators (businesses)
Older and disabled passengers who rely on taxis

items.title: Port Talbot Steelworks: draft permit decision (PAN-029148.1)
items.time: closing time not published; the consultation page says it closes 13 November 2026.
items.plain: Tata Steel is changing the steelworks permit as it moves from blast furnaces to an electric arc furnace. NRW is minded to approve this first stage and wants comments on the draft permit.
items.detail: Names Port Talbot directly: the site is Port Talbot Steelworks, SA13 2NG, and NRW lists Aberavon, Baglan, Bryn and Cwmavon, Margam, Port Talbot, Sandfields East and West and Tai-bach among the areas covered. This variation (V019 of permit EPR/BL7108IM) removes blast furnace and basic oxygen steelmaking activities, mothballs others during the transformation and adds new steam boilers (medium combustion plant). NRW says it can only consider comments within its legal permitting remit. Later stages, including the electric arc furnace itself, will be consulted on separately.
items.how: Comment online through NRW Citizen Space, or email permittingconsultations@naturalresourceswales.gov.uk, by 13 November 2026.

people: Residents of Aberavon, Baglan, Margam, Sandfields and Tai-bach near the site
systems: Air quality and emissions from the works

items.title: Afan Forest draft Forest Resource Plan
items.time: closing time not published; NRW says the consultation runs from 1 to 30 November. Drop-in session 11 November 2026, 1pm to 7pm, Afan Visitor Centre, Cynonville.
items.plain: NRW sets out how it plans to manage Afan Forest for the next 10 years: timber, nature recovery, climate resilience and recreation, including the mountain bike trails.
items.detail: Names Neath Port Talbot places: the plan covers the Afan, Pelenna, Corrwg and Drysiog catchments, with a drop-in at Afan Visitor Centre, Cynonville, Port Talbot. Proposals include more diverse woodland, better ecological connectivity, restoring peatland and ancient woodland, managing invasive species, improving river habitats and protecting water and soil. The year of the 30 November close is taken from the 2026 drop-in date in the same NRW news release.
items.how: View the documents and respond online (link in the NRW news release), go to the drop-in on 11 November, or email frp@cyfoethnaturiolcymru.gov.uk.

people: Forest businesses and mountain bike tourism

items.title: Revising the National Development Framework
items.time: closing time not published; the consultation page says it ends 20 November 2026.
items.plain: The Welsh Government is starting to revise Wales's national planning framework, and asks how people want to take part and what the new framework should do.
items.detail: Applies to all of Wales; it does not name a Neath Port Talbot place. Kept because the National Development Framework guides large developments, energy and growth areas across Wales, including this county borough. It covers the draft Statement of Public Participation, the draft National Conversation Engagement Plan and the role of the revised framework.
items.how: Respond online, or email the response form to planconsultations-h@gov.wales, or post it to the Planning Directorate, Welsh Government, Cathays Park, Cardiff CF10 3NQ, by 20 November 2026.

people: Landowners and businesses near future development

items.title: Shaping Mid and West Wales Fire and Rescue Service Together
items.body: Mid and West Wales Fire and Rescue Service
items.time: No closing date is published on the survey page, so the days count is a placeholder. Check the page.
items.plain: A short anonymous survey about what you expect from your fire and rescue service and what it should prioritise.
items.detail: Covers the whole Mid and West Wales fire service area, which includes Neath Port Talbot; the page does not name Neath Port Talbot specifically. No closing date is published, so check the page before relying on it being open. The survey includes an optional prize draw.
items.how: Fill in the online survey from the service's page, or ring 0370 6060699 for another language or format.

people: Every resident in the fire service area
Older and vulnerable people who rely on fire safety visits

items.title: Let's Talk: Living in NPT survey
items.body: Neath Port Talbot Council (run by the Welsh Local Government Association)
items.plain: The council's yearly residents' survey on services, local priorities and life in your area.
items.detail: Open to Neath Port Talbot residents aged 16 or over; closed on 27 October 2026. No results or outcome had been published by 3 November 2026. The council publishes what it did with last year's results on its 'Have your say' pages.
items.how: The survey has closed. Watch the council's consultations page for the results.
